claims.text: The starting material is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy has favorable plasticity and machinability.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy has relatively low room-temperature hardness and strength.
Friction-stir severe plastic deformation activates deformation-induced nanotwinning in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Friction-stir severe plastic deformation can induce nucleation of a minor HCP phase in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanotwins and strain-induced HCP regions are absent from the as-cast FCC starting state.
The SPD-induced nanotwins and HCP transformation are responsible for the alloy's relatively low hardness and strength.
Severe plastic deformation introduces copious dislocations and localized internal stresses.
Dislocation activity and localized stresses trigger nanotwinning.
Dislocation activity and localized stresses trigger a partial FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Nanotwins and HCP regions increase barriers to dislocation motion.
The SPD-induced microstructural features enhance work hardening.
The as-cast state lacks sufficient microstructural obstacles, causing lower hardness and strength while retaining good plasticity.
SPD-processed CoCrFeNiTi will have greater hardness than the untreated alloy.
SPD-processed CoCrFeNiTi will have greater strength than the untreated alloy.
TEM of the SPD-processed alloy will reveal a high density of nanotwins.
TEM may reveal small strain-induced HCP regions in the SPD-processed alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-FCC-phase CoCrFeNiTi under ambient quasi-static to moderate strain-rate loading.
The proposed effect requires deformation temperatures low enough to avoid significant recovery or recrystallization.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says SPD-induced nanotwins and HCP regions are responsible for the relatively low hardness and strength, whereas the mechanism and prediction say these same features raise barriers to dislocation motion and increase hardness and strength.

The mediator is stated as nanotwins and/or HCP, the prediction describes HCP only as possible, and the uncertainty allows HCP to be unmeasurable; nevertheless, failure to detect a distinct HCP phase is presented as sufficient to falsify the mechanism.
